args.text: [lane-heron] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: if a site moves to a new server, users keep being sent to the old one, causing outages or errors. (2) Slow failover: when traffic must be redirected during a fault, the old answer lingers, so recovery takes longer. (3) Prolonged poisoning: if a forged answer is cached, it stays in use for longer, so harm lasts well past the attack itself.

[lane-heron] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again. If repeating the request gives the same result as sending it once, a retry cannot cause double charges, duplicate records or other unwanted side effects.

[lane-heron] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) Larger keys: it takes more storage than a plain whole-number key, so indexes grow and lookups can be slower. (2) Leaked creation time: the start of each value encodes when it was made, so outsiders can infer record age or rough activity levels.

[lane-heron] A write-ahead log (WAL) is an append-only record where a database writes each change to durable storage before applying it to the main data files. After a crash, the system replays this log to restore a consistent state, so no committed change is lost and no half-finished change is kept.

[lane-heron] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a client update can change speed or behaviour on its own, so unpinned runs may show differences that have nothing to do with the thing being tested. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the same set-up later and get comparable results, because the software under test has not shifted.
